content.text: [Slack #legal-review sarah Thu Mar 12 10:00 EST 2026] Quick update: I reviewed the external audit letter. Their recommendation to use 'Results Not Typical' is wrong. That safe harbor was definitively abolished in the 2009 revision to the Endorsement Guides and has NOT been restored in the 2023 revision. Section §255.2 now requires advertisers to prove what results consumers generally achieve, not merely disclaim atypical results. Any compliance report should categorize the 'Results Not Typical' recommendation from the first audit letter as superseded law and discard it.

Confirmed. The first audit letter's 'Results Not Typical' recommendation is based on the 1980/pre-2009 Guides and constitutes superseded law. Per §255.2 (2023), the safe harbor no longer exists. This will be classified as a superseded_recommendation in Q10 output (along with any reliance on the 1998 Dietary Supplements Guide).
